link.host_enable: Let paired machines connect to this one
link.host_hint: Off by default. When on, this machine listens for connections from machines you have paired with, and your firewall will ask once.
link.portmap_mapped: Your router opened the port automatically ({via}). Invites now carry {address}, so this machine is reachable from another network.
link.portmap_unsupported: Your router did not answer automatic port opening (UPnP / NAT-PMP). Connections from this network still work. From elsewhere, use the IPv6 address above, an overlay network, or turn UPnP on in the router.
link.portmap_carrier: Your router opened the port, but your ISP puts it behind carrier-grade NAT — the address behind it is not reachable from the internet. Use the IPv6 address above, or an overlay network.
link.portmap_failed: Your router refused to open the port: {detail}
link.create_code_hint: One code, valid for five minutes, usable once. It carries this machine’s address and identity, so nothing has to be typed on the other side.
link.paste_on_other: Copy this and paste it on the other machine.
link.no_devices: No machine has been paired with this one yet.
link.no_machines: No other machines yet. Create a code on the machine you want to reach, then paste it here.
link.clipboard_found: Found a connection code for {name} in your clipboard.
link.err_unreachable: Nothing answered at {addresses}. The machine may be asleep, on another network, or blocked by its firewall.
link.err_tls: Something answered, but the two DevDecks could not agree on how to talk. Check that both are up to date.
link.err_fingerprint: The machine that answered is not the one you paired with. This is either a different machine at that address, or someone in the middle. Nothing was sent to it.
link.err_unpaired: That machine no longer allows this one in. Create a new code on it.
link.err_expired: That code has expired. Codes last five minutes — create a new one on the other machine.
link.err_version: The two machines are running different DevDeck versions. Update both.
link.err_not_a_code: That is not a connection code. Copy the whole line, starting with DDLINK1.
link.err_truncated: That code looks cut off. Copy the whole line and paste it again.
link.err_malformed: That code could not be read. Create a new one on the other machine.

diag.title: Diagnostics log
link.err_unreachable_head: None of this machine's addresses answered:
link.dial_refused: connection refused (the machine is up, nothing listening there)
link.dial_timed-out: no answer (the route exists; the packets went nowhere)
link.dial_tls: connected, but the two ends could not agree on security
link.advice_no-ipv6-here: The only addresses reachable from another network are IPv6, and this machine has no IPv6 route. No setting on the other machine can fix that — this one needs a network with IPv6, or an overlay such as Tailscale at both ends.
link.advice_far-side-blocking: There IS a route to the IPv6 address and nothing answered on it. The other machine's router is blocking inbound connections, or that machine is asleep.
link.advice_same-network-only: Every address offered only works inside that machine's own network. It had no address to give that reaches it from outside.

whatsnew.title: What's new in DevDeck {version}
whatsnew.subtitle: Recent changes, and where to find each one.
whatsnew.need_session: Open a Claude session first — this lives in a session's header.
whatsnew.not_found: That setting is not available on this computer.
whatsnew.f.program-status.title: Claude tells DevDeck what it is doing
whatsnew.f.program-status.body: Working, done, needs approval or asking a question — straight from Claude Code instead of guessed from the screen. The session header shows it, with what it just did.
whatsnew.f.program-status.where: Settings → Claude status signal (experimental), then start a new session
whatsnew.f.quick-replies.title: Quick replies
whatsnew.f.quick-replies.body: Send "Yes, go ahead", "Commit it" and your own phrases in one click, or with Ctrl+Shift+1…9.
whatsnew.f.quick-replies.where: The 💬 button in a session's header
whatsnew.f.timeline.title: Session timeline
whatsnew.f.timeline.body: Every prompt you sent, with its time, the reply and its screenshots. Click one to jump there.
whatsnew.f.timeline.where: The timeline button in a session's header
whatsnew.f.image-markup.title: Mark up a screenshot and send it back
whatsnew.f.image-markup.body: Draw red boxes and arrows on a screenshot, then attach it to the session in one click.
whatsnew.f.remote-documents.title: Documents for a session on another PC
whatsnew.f.remote-documents.body: Text, log, data and PDF files now travel too, not only images.
whatsnew.f.remote-documents.where: 📎 or drag and drop onto a remote session
whatsnew.f.image-rows.title: Which step was this screenshot?
whatsnew.f.image-rows.body: [Image] rows in the terminal are highlighted: hover for a thumbnail, click to open. The viewer shows what led to each image and can jump back to its row, or copy it.
whatsnew.f.image-rows.where: Highlighted [Image] rows, and the image viewer
whatsnew.f.prompt-jump.title: Jump between your prompts
whatsnew.f.prompt-jump.body: Step back and forward through the prompts you sent in a long session.
whatsnew.f.image-strip.title: Screenshots beside the terminal
whatsnew.f.image-strip.body: The screenshots and images a Claude session worked with, as thumbnails — also for sessions on another PC.
whatsnew.f.image-strip.where: The image button in a session's header
whatsnew.f.update-all.title: Update all Claude sessions at once
whatsnew.f.update-all.body: When Claude Code has an update, one button stops every session, updates it and brings the same conversations back.
whatsnew.f.update-all.where: Appears in the session header when an update is waiting
cockpit.worktree_new: New session in a separate workspace (its own git branch and folder)
cockpit.worktree_failed: Could not create a separate workspace — {reason}
cockpit.worktree_host_too_old: DevDeck on {machine} is too old for separate workspaces — update it to 1.43.0.
cockpit.worktree_pill_title: A separate workspace: its own folder and git branch, so it never touches the project's other sessions.
cockpit.worktree_cleanup_clean: Close this session and delete its workspace folder and branch {branch}? It holds no changes of its own.
cockpit.worktree_cleanup_losing: This workspace holds {what}. Cleaning up deletes them with the folder and branch {branch}. To keep them, cancel and ask a session on {base} to merge {branch} first.
cockpit.worktree_unknown: This workspace was not created by this DevDeck, so it is left alone.
whatsnew.f.worktree-sessions.title: Parallel sessions in separate workspaces
whatsnew.f.worktree-sessions.body: Start another session on the same project in its own folder and git branch, so two agents never edit the same files. The header shows what it has changed; cleaning up warns before anything unmerged is lost.
whatsnew.f.worktree-sessions.where: The branch button in a session's header
whatsnew.f.send-any-file.title: Send any file to a session on another PC
whatsnew.f.send-any-file.body: Zip, spreadsheet, source file, video: any kind, up to 4 GB (it was 21 document kinds, 5 MB). Large files go in pieces with their progress shown.
whatsnew.f.send-any-file.where: The 📎 button in a remote session's header, or drop onto its terminal
whatsnew.f.background-agents.title: Claude's background sessions in the sidebar
whatsnew.f.background-agents.body: Sessions started with claude --bg or from Claude's agent view now show up, with the ones waiting for you marked. Click one to open it in a tile; it keeps running as it was.
whatsnew.f.background-agents.where: The "Claude background sessions" group in the sidebar
